target_customer: Mobile gamers, especially heavy spenders in free-to-play strategy games; later game developers via its connectivity platform
problem: Mobile games lacked deep real-time multiplayer play; the company built free-to-play games with live players and monetized a small share of heavy payers.
business_model: free-to-play in-app purchases, plus ad buying and a data platform side businesses

founders.name: Gabriel Leydon
founders.background_notes: Left mid-2018 to lead the Satori spinoff, per search summary

competitors.name: Mob Wars and similar social mob games
competitors.what: social network mafia games that iMob Online imitated for iPhone
competitors.traction_then: popular on Facebook and MySpace in 2008 to 2009

technical_complexity.rationale: Early games were standard iOS development; later real-time global multiplayer at scale was harder.

defensibility.rationale: Game mechanics were copyable, defensibility came from player communities, user acquisition spend and live ops.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No incumbent bought it early; it was sold to AppLovin in 2020 after its peak had passed.

market_need_then: The iPhone App Store opened in 2008 and TechCrunch noted appetite for Mob Wars style games, with Machine Zone reaching nearly 40 million downloads by 2012.

branding.name_origin: Originally Addmired, after widgets AddHer and AddHim; renamed Machine Zone in 2012, no reason given at the time. Leydon later said the old name confused new hires.
branding.brand_signature: Celebrity ad campaigns for Game of War with Kate Upton and Arnold Schwarzenegger, including a 2015 Super Bowl spot

rebrands.why: Old name confused staff and did not fit games, per founder remarks
Rebranded as MZ with a standalone tech platform, per press release title

branding.community_and_virality: Celebrity ads for Game of War were widely covered in press.

brand_strength.rationale: Game of War was heavily advertised and famous but the company brand itself was less known.

pivots.why: Games monetized better, per TechCrunch coverage of Addmired's iMob launch

outcome_analysis: Machine Zone pivoted from social widgets to iPhone mob games in 2009, raised an $8M round in 2012, then reached huge scale with Game of War backed by celebrity advertising and a reported multibillion valuation in 2014 to 2016. Later it shrank, shut its ad platform and was bought by AppLovin in May 2020 for a disputed price.
notes: mz.com returned HTTP 503 during this run. Series B $8M confirmed by TechCrunch, PRNewswire and Game Developer; its date is March 2012. A Series A of $5.3M in 2011 and a 2014 round near $250M with JPMorgan and valuations of $3B to $5B appear only in aggregators and unconfirmed reports, so not recorded as rounds. AppLovin price conflicts: about $330M (MarketScreener), about $500M (wiki mirror), undisclosed (PocketGamer), so null. Deal agreed 2020-05-14, closed 2020-05-19 per one source. Tripledot bought AppLovin's games portfolio in 2025 (reported). The 2018 MZ rebrand date is inferred from the press release title and not verified. Leydon and Sherrill backgrounds not retrieved.
